#### 5.12.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** unreadable resource feedback, ecological oversimplification. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `branching root stars shine through translucent soil slices; L-system miniature flora, deterministic boids, bioluminescence and simple water planes` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/root-constellation/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/root-constellation/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/root-constellation/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. **Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 13. Lichen Cathedral — complete proposed implementation design (`R10-G13`)
**Source:** `G279`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.59 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Grow patterned lichen across 3D arches according to moisture rules. **Signature animated environment:** branching radial colonies spread over curved stone surfaces; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials. **Core abstraction:** branching growth grammar.
#### 5.13.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees branching radial colonies spread over curved stone surfaces; recursive l-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Grow patterned lichen across 3D arches according to moisture rules. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `branching growth grammar` computational rules, visual `branching radial colonies spread over curved stone surfaces; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials` and player control arrangement `Grow/prune branching organisms to satisfy spatial or timing constraints`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.13.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** rewrite L-system symbol grammar with seed, branch budget and nutrient constraints. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Grow patterned lichen across 3D arches according to moisture rules. Normalize input into `LichenCathedralAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** guide branching structure to supply target nodes or form a defined canopy. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 8 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over pruning/branch-choice states and growth feasibility. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** exploding node counts, aliasing branches, impossible pruning. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.13.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting branching radial colonies spread over curved stone surfaces; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable branching growth grammar handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with grow patterned lichen across 3d arches according to moisture rules; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative branching growth grammar predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Grow/prune branching organisms to satisfy spatial or timing constraints. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.13.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** tube branch sweep, instanced leaves, procedural subsurface-look tint. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** branching radial colonies spread over curved stone surfaces; Recursive L-systems, instanced leaves, flow network evolution and bioluminescent materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `LichenCathedralScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `LichenCathedralParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `7b8a339c77e7` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.13.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct branching growth grammar controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 14. Glacier Sculptor — complete proposed implementation design (`R10-G14`)
**Source:** `G323`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.59 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Route slow-moving ice to connect isolated valleys. **Signature animated environment:** translucent-looking ice ridges and dynamic fracture lines; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. **Core abstraction:** heightfield energy transport.
#### 5.14.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees translucent-looking ice ridges and dynamic fracture lines; deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Route slow-moving ice to connect isolated valleys. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `heightfield energy transport` computational rules, visual `translucent-looking ice ridges and dynamic fracture lines; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky` and player control arrangement `Reshape terrain to redirect natural flows or light`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.14.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** h_next=clamp(h+sculpt, h_min,h_max); finite-volume erosion conserves removed material. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Route slow-moving ice to connect isolated valleys. Normalize input into `GlacierSculptorAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** reshape terrain until flow, silhouette or shading goals are satisfied. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** coarse-grid A* on discretized height steps and flow destination validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** terrain cliffs, mesh cracks, GPU overdraw. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.14.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting translucent-looking ice ridges and dynamic fracture lines; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable heightfield energy transport handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with route slow-moving ice to connect isolated valleys; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative heightfield energy transport predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Reshape terrain to redirect natural flows or light. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.14.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** heightfield tessellation, generated normals, gradient atmospheres. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** translucent-looking ice ridges and dynamic fracture lines; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `GlacierSculptorScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `GlacierSculptorParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `e0cd4827eb19` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.14.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 15. Terrace Rivers — complete proposed implementation design (`R10-G15`)
**Source:** `G325`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.59 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Carve terraces that carry water through three target gardens. **Signature animated environment:** cascading low-cost water ribbons between sculpted plateaus; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. **Core abstraction:** heightfield energy transport.
#### 5.15.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees cascading low-cost water ribbons between sculpted plateaus; deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Carve terraces that carry water through three target gardens. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `heightfield energy transport` computational rules, visual `cascading low-cost water ribbons between sculpted plateaus; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky` and player control arrangement `Reshape terrain to redirect natural flows or light`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.15.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** h_next=clamp(h+sculpt, h_min,h_max); finite-volume erosion conserves removed material. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Carve terraces that carry water through three target gardens. Normalize input into `TerraceRiversAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** reshape terrain until flow, silhouette or shading goals are satisfied. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** coarse-grid A* on discretized height steps and flow destination validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** terrain cliffs, mesh cracks, GPU overdraw. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.15.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting cascading low-cost water ribbons between sculpted plateaus; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable heightfield energy transport handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with carve terraces that carry water through three target gardens; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative heightfield energy transport predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Reshape terrain to redirect natural flows or light. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.15.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** heightfield tessellation, generated normals, gradient atmospheres. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** cascading low-cost water ribbons between sculpted plateaus; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `TerraceRiversScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `TerraceRiversParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `9859ef9b0bd5` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.15.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct heightfield energy transport controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 16. Crankwave Lab — complete proposed implementation design (`R10-G16`)
**Source:** `G350`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.58 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Tune linkages to produce a specified three-dimensional wave trajectory. **Signature animated environment:** mechanical arms draw ribbons of colored light; Fixed-step rigid primitives, parametric gears, spring joints and trailing glow. **Core abstraction:** constrained kinematic graph.
#### 5.16.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees mechanical arms draw ribbons of colored light; fixed-step rigid primitives, parametric gears, spring joints and trailing glow, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Tune linkages to produce a specified three-dimensional wave trajectory. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `constrained kinematic graph` computational rules, visual `mechanical arms draw ribbons of colored light; Fixed-step rigid primitives, parametric gears, spring joints and trailing glow` and player control arrangement `Tune mechanism geometry or phase to satisfy a timed pattern`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.16.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** joint angles θ_i follow bounded tick-indexed harmonic driving signals. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Tune linkages to produce a specified three-dimensional wave trajectory. Normalize input into `CrankwaveLabAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** synchronize mechanisms through a target pose/time window. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** joint phase enumeration plus swept geometry collision and stability tests. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** mechanical collisions, numerical chatter, inaccessible rotation controls. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.16.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting mechanical arms draw ribbons of colored light; Fixed-step rigid primitives, parametric gears, spring joints and trailing glow; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable constrained kinematic graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with tune linkages to produce a specified three-dimensional wave trajectory; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative constrained kinematic graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tune mechanism geometry or phase to satisfy a timed pattern. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.16.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** faceted gears, rotating torus paths and emissive motion traces. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** mechanical arms draw ribbons of colored light; Fixed-step rigid primitives, parametric gears, spring joints and trailing glow. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `CrankwaveLabScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `CrankwaveLabParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `1235c66c1b32` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.16.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct constrained kinematic graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.16.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** mechanical collisions, numerical chatter, inaccessible rotation controls. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `mechanical arms draw ribbons of colored light; Fixed-step rigid primitives, parametric gears, spring joints and trailing glow` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/crankwave-lab/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/crankwave-lab/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/crankwave-lab/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 17. Volcano Glassworks — complete proposed implementation design (`R10-G17`)
**Source:** `G322`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.57 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Dig channels to cool lava into a prescribed geometric structure. **Signature animated environment:** emissive viscous-looking lava streams over black volcanic slopes; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. **Core abstraction:** heightfield energy transport.
#### 5.17.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees emissive viscous-looking lava streams over black volcanic slopes; deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Dig channels to cool lava into a prescribed geometric structure. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `heightfield energy transport` computational rules, visual `emissive viscous-looking lava streams over black volcanic slopes; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky` and player control arrangement `Reshape terrain to redirect natural flows or light`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.17.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** h_next=clamp(h+sculpt, h_min,h_max); finite-volume erosion conserves removed material. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Dig channels to cool lava into a prescribed geometric structure. Normalize input into `VolcanoGlassworksAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** reshape terrain until flow, silhouette or shading goals are satisfied. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** coarse-grid A* on discretized height steps and flow destination validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** terrain cliffs, mesh cracks, GPU overdraw. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.17.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting emissive viscous-looking lava streams over black volcanic slopes; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable heightfield energy transport handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with dig channels to cool lava into a prescribed geometric structure; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative heightfield energy transport predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Reshape terrain to redirect natural flows or light. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.17.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** heightfield tessellation, generated normals, gradient atmospheres. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** emissive viscous-looking lava streams over black volcanic slopes; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `VolcanoGlassworksScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `VolcanoGlassworksParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `36b5bf630cc9` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.

#### 5.17.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** terrain cliffs, mesh cracks, GPU overdraw. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `emissive viscous-looking lava streams over black volcanic slopes; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/volcano-glassworks/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/volcano-glassworks/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND10_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round10/volcano-glassworks/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. ### 18. Rainchain Atelier — complete proposed implementation design (`R10-G18`)
**Source:** `G237`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **92.57 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Construct suspended drip chains that strike bells in a required rhythm. **Signature animated environment:** sparkling procedural rain beads and glossy linking curves; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials. **Core abstraction:** conservative transport grid.
#### 5.18.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees sparkling procedural rain beads and glossy linking curves; cpu heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking glsl materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Construct suspended drip chains that strike bells in a required rhythm. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `conservative transport grid` computational rules, visual `sparkling procedural rain beads and glossy linking curves; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials` and player control arrangement `Steer streams through obstacles into deterministic targets`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.18.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** q_next=q+inflow-outflow; Σq drift<=1e-8 in double CPU tests. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Construct suspended drip chains that strike bells in a required rhythm. Normalize input into `RainchainAtelierAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** redirect a finite amount of fluid to specified reservoirs while limiting pollution. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** deterministic coarse-grid flow search + mass conservation assertions. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** CFL instability, visual physics differing from actual solver. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.18.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting sparkling procedural rain beads and glossy linking curves; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable conservative transport grid handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with construct suspended drip chains that strike bells in a required rhythm; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative conservative transport grid predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Steer streams through obstacles into deterministic targets. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.18.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** animated flow maps on generated terrain and emissive velocity filaments. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** sparkling procedural rain beads and glossy linking curves; CPU heightfield/velocity fields, ribbon meshes and transparent-looking GLSL materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `RainchainAtelierScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `RainchainAtelierParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `6a9ed910fcca` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.18.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct conservative transport grid controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.
